title: Embedding Living Larvae in Low-Melting Agarose for Imaging and Recovery
author: Pringle Lab
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qxbdxin

steps.title: Melt agarose aliquot
steps.instruction: Melt a 1 ml aliquot of 2 % low‑melting agarose stock at 65 °C in a water bath or heat block; melting takes a few minutes (longer for a 50 ml tube). Use this stock to obtain a final 1 % agarose concentration; higher stock concentrations up to 8 % are possible but make pipetting difficult.

steps.title: Keep agarose liquid
steps.instruction: Transfer the melted agarose to a 37 °C heat block (or keep in a 37 °C water bath) so it remains liquid and ready for use.

steps.title: Prepare slide and coverslip
steps.instruction: Label a microscope slide, place a coverslip equipped with clay feet beside it, and set both next to the stereomicroscope.

steps.title: Collect larvae in ASW
steps.instruction: Under the stereomicroscope, transfer 5–10 µl of artificial seawater (ASW) containing up to 10 larvae into a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube and close the lid; larger volumes do not fit under standard 18 × 18 mm coverslips.

steps.title: Set second pipette volume
steps.instruction: Adjust a second micropipette to a volume equal to twice the volume of the larval suspension (e.g., if the suspension is 10 µl, set the pipette to 20 µl).

steps.title: Position slide for imaging
steps.instruction: Place the labeled slide under the stereomicroscope and adjust focus and magnification so the future larval positions will be visible.

steps.title: Mix larvae with agarose
steps.instruction: Place the 37 °C agarose next to the stereomicroscope; if desired, use a 27 °C heat block and wait a few minutes, but do not let the agarose solidify. Add an equal volume of agarose to the larval suspension (1:1 ratio) and gently pipette up and down several times to mix immediately.

steps.title: Apply mixture and coverslip
steps.instruction: Using the second pipette, transfer the entire agarose‑larvae mixture onto the slide; while observing through the microscope, place the clay‑foot coverslip on top and press lightly to create a layer roughly the thickness of the larvae. Ensure all larvae remain under the coverslip, avoid excessive squeezing, and keep the coverslip resting on its clay feet.

steps.title: Seal slide edges
steps.instruction: Add a small amount of 2 % agarose to the edges of the coverslip to fill the area beneath, then seal the edges airtight with hot Valap.

steps.title: Check positions and image
steps.instruction: After sealing, examine the larvae again under the stereomicroscope; optionally mark their positions with dots on the coverslip to aid later identification with a compound microscope. Acquire images—larvae remain viable for 2–4 hours.

steps.title: Remove coverslip and recover larvae
steps.instruction: Under the stereomicroscope, (1) use a razor blade, scalpel, or another coverslip to cut away wax around the sample; (2) carefully lift the coverslip with a scalpel blade, keeping the sample moist; (3) place the removed coverslip upside‑down on a clean surface and cover both the coverslip and the slide area with ASW; (4) locate larvae with a micropipette and transfer them back to their dish. If some larvae remain embedded, wait for them to free themselves or transfer them together with the small agarose piece.
